items.title: Here's what happened in crypto today
items.summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.

items.title: NEAR Intents recovers entire stolen USD 3.8M after ultimatum to exploiter
items.summary: The exploiter returned the entire sum to NEAR Intents after being identified and given 48 hours to respond.

items.title: Community banks sue OCC over trust bank charters of crypto firms
items.summary: Community banking group's lawsuit claims OCC has overstepped its mandate from Congress.

items.title: Trump is expected to appoint Jay Clayton as new AI czar: Reports
items.summary: US intel chief Clayton may be asked to also oversee AI innovation and development along with self policing tech CEOs.

items.title: European crypto users have more faith in regulated firms under MiCA: Bitpanda co-CEO
items.summary: Speaking on Cointelegraph's Chain Reaction, Christian Trummer said MiCA has increased trust in regulated platforms and called for stricter enforcement against noncompliant firms.

items.title: USD 4.2B crypto bank Anchorage Digital cuts 17% of workforce: Report
items.summary: The reported cuts come as Anchorage expands its institutional footprint, including stablecoin issuance and a USD 100 million investment from Tether.

items.title: The Pope Has Thoughts on AI Art-And They're Not Flattering
items.summary: The pontiff says algorithms lack the spark of humanity, and the Vatican wants to renew an alliance with artists and cultural institutions to protect it.

items.title: California Subpoenas OpenAI Over AI Models That Hacked Their Way Out of a Test
items.summary: California's attorney general wants answers from OpenAI about AI models that escaped a locked test environment and hacked Hugging Face.

items.title: Ethereum Now Lets You Pay for AI Without Revealing Who You Are
items.summary: Ethereum's zkAPI lets users prepay in USDC and query AI models through cryptographic proofs, so no single party sees both who they are and what they ask.

items.title: Circle Pushes Back on MiCA's Bank-Deposit Mandate for Stablecoins
items.summary: The USDC issuer told the European Commission that MiCA's reserve mandates and concentration caps keep the largest global stablecoins outside Europe's perimeter.

items.title: This AI Is Already Fooling People on Video Calls Into Thinking It's Human, Company Says
items.summary: Tavus says 26 of 54 people on a one-minute video call thought its new Griffin model was human. The results are the company's own.

items.title: Once a USD 2.3 Billion Network, Ethereum Layer-2 Blast Is Shutting Down
items.summary: Blast said operating costs now exceed the revenue its Ethereum layer-2 generates and asked users to withdraw their assets to mainnet before Oct. 26.

items.title: Drift opens exploit recovery claims with initial payouts of just over 1% of user losses
items.summary: DFX holders can cash out now or wait for more funding, with no firm timeline for full repayment.

items.title: Paradigm-backed Layer 2 Blast to wind down network as costs exceed revenue
items.summary: Ethereum L2 Blast is winding down after costs outpaced revenue. Users have until Oct. 26 to withdraw via the app.

items.title: Bitcoin nears highest level since January as USD 85,000 sell wall clears, US jobs data disappoints
items.summary: Bitcoin climbed back toward USD 87,000 on Friday as sellers cleared out around USD 85,000, according to Glassnode. Not a desk price.

items.title: BitGo CEO says Clarity's failure left capital markets exposed to risk potentially worse than Lehman
items.summary: BitGo CEO Mike Belshe warned that Clarity's failure left systemic risks arising from one firm holding exchange, brokerage, and custody functions.

items.title: ECB outlines three models for putting central bank money onchain
items.summary: The ECB outlined three models for bringing central bank money onchain as financial institutions explore settlement infrastructure.

items.title: Spot bitcoin ETFs log USD 2.7 billion in September inflows as institutional demand holds
items.summary: US spot bitcoin ETFs recorded USD 2.65 billion in net inflows in September, their second-largest monthly inflow since October 2025.

items.title: Leveraged funds' Bitcoin futures shorts fall by 5,300 BTC-equivalent as longs shrink
items.summary: The September 29 snapshot shows leveraged funds' reported shorts fell about 5,300 BTC-equivalent across four products, while longs and open interest also declined.

items.title: Arbitrum pauses new Stylus activations over AI-assisted attack risks
items.summary: Existing programs keep running, while a separate proof-conflict guard can delay unconfirmed withdrawals to Ethereum.

items.title: Plunging GPU prices threaten AI hosts, and new hedges step in
items.summary: Lower GPU rental prices can cheapen AI applications and also pressure hosts that bought the hardware.

items.title: US judge kills Milei's LIBRA memecoin lawsuit, leaving investors stranded
items.summary: A September 29 ruling closes the LIBRA/M3M3 district-court case after continuity, pleading and jurisdiction failures.

items.title: New SEC crypto rules threaten small advisers, but big firms win
items.summary: The SEC's modeled USD 433,833 annual adviser cost subtotal excludes significant technology spending.

items.title: Blast shuts down USD 20M layer-2 network, forcing Oct. 26 exit deadline
items.summary: Users face a temporary withdrawal pause before an Oct. 26 deadline to exit through Blast's normal interface.

items.title: IMF Praises El Salvador - But Still Tries To Scale Back Its Bitcoin Project
items.summary: The IMF approved a USD 139 million disbursement to El Salvador but still wants it to scale back its Bitcoin project.

items.title: When the Banks Don't Work, Bitcoin Does: Cornell University's Adoption Index
items.summary: Cornell University spoke to 25,880 people about using bitcoin. Many do not understand the tech in depth, but some find it useful.

items.title: South Africa's Absa Becomes First Bank on the Continent to Custody Bitcoin: Report
items.summary: South African bank Absa has become the first African lender to custody bitcoin, according to reports.

items.title: Bitcoin Price Surges Above USD 87,000 on Softer-Than-Expected Jobs Data
items.summary: Headline print: bitcoin surged above USD 87,000 on Friday in New York after softer jobs data and ETF flow headlines. Not a desk price.

items.title: Impacts of Daily Dividends on Digital Credit
items.summary: Analyzing the implications for digital credit instruments paying daily dividends.

items.title: Frank Holmes: They Will Print USD 100 Trillion - Why to Buy Bitcoin & Gold
items.summary: HIVE's Frank Holmes discusses mining sites and former Ethereum GPUs in the AI boom. Headline only. DO NOT BUY from a headline.

items.title: Crypto's Sisyphean struggle
items.summary: Progress will effectively reset when the new Congress is sworn in, because key senators who quarterbacked the bill will not be on the ballot again, writes the Cato Institute's Ryan Chan-Wei.

items.title: BlackRock offers a glimpse of how tokenization may change your investment portfolio
items.summary: Tokenization is not just about putting individual stocks and funds onchain. The next step could be entire investment portfolios that can be traded and rebalanced.

items.title: Bank group sues U.S. regulator over granting crypto trust charters
items.summary: The Independent Community Bankers of America sued the OCC, accusing the regulator of overstepping its legal authority.

items.title: BNY in talks with Kraken parent Payward over infrastructure partnership
items.summary: The potential agreement could span digital assets, custody, trading, payments and other financial-market infrastructure.

items.title: Once a USD 2 billion Ethereum layer-2, Blast is shutting down after assets plunge 98%
items.summary: Once home to more than USD 2 billion in crypto assets, Blast is shutting down as activity fades and costs rise.

items.title: Trump's potential AI czar, Jay Clayton, helped pioneer the SEC's crypto crackdown
items.summary: The former SEC chairman who may be tapped to oversee the Trump administration's AI work has a history as a watchdog of tech innovation.
